Source contracts: scripts/code_quality

scripts/code_quality/guidance_guard.py

Python · Tier B

Check exact implemented text against an immutable Git revision.

Details

The static check includes every string literal in product Python, not just names containing 'prompt' or 'guidance'. It also protects instruction resources and the existing guidance fixtures. No inspected package is imported or executed.

@see scripts/code_quality/README.md

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
protected 51 Include instruction owners and fixtures, excluding third-party and test code.
literal_fingerprints 65 Count exact string values, including docstrings, without emitting their text. Multiplicity prevents replacing one existing instruction with another. Literal spelling may change, but spaces, newlines, Unicode and f-string fragments must remain exact. Order and interpolation are covered separately by request tests and executable-AST comparisons for mechanical changes.
unchanged_shell_help 85 Allow a leading comment header only when help bytes and shell code stay exact. release.sh prints a fixed line range from its own comments. Inserting file documentation must shift both ends of that range by the same line count. Everything after the inserted comments remains byte-for-byte protected.
compare 117 Reject missing files or changed text; comments outside literals may change.
git 148 Read Git through an argument vector, without interpreting source as shell code.
reviewed_documentation_additions 155 Accept only exact reviewed new README bytes, never existing instruction changes. A manifest is tied to one starting commit. Every listed addition must be a new protected README, stay within the checkout, and retain its reviewed hash. The reason records why the owning loader does not consume it as guidance.
reviewed_documentation_updates 193 Accept exact before/after reviews for existing protected folder READMEs. The human review must establish that the owning loader does not consume the README as instructions. Both hashes bind that decision to one concrete edit; no other resource name, later edit, removal or symlink is exempted.
check 242 Check original protected paths and flag new instruction owners for review.
main 301 Print content-free findings and fail on any protected-text change.

scripts/code_quality/import_boundary_report.py

Python · Tier B

Inspect Python import directions without importing repository packages.

Usage

Run as scripts.code_quality.import_boundary_report from the repository root.

Inputs

Git-listed source text and the reviewed boundary rules JSON.

Side effects

Reads source/Git metadata and prints deterministic JSON; never boots a service.

Cleanup

Git subprocesses finish before return; no application resources are opened.

@see scripts/code_quality/README.md

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
maintained_python 42 Use path components, preserving artifacts and execution_cache product packages.
git 54 Read Git metadata/content with arguments, never shell interpolation.
working_paths 63 Include tracked files and nonignored additions, without dependency-tree traversal.
safe_source 76 Exclude symlinks and virtual environments even when their files are tracked.
sources 87 Read only maintained Python candidates; source text is parsed, never executed.
module_name 96 Map the repository src layout, including its nested inference distribution.
import_edges 106 Distinguish syntactic eager, function-local lazy and TYPE_CHECKING edges. This is not import execution: implicit parent initialization, dynamic imports, platform conditions and arbitrary aliases require separate human review.
forbidden_edges 170 Match module boundaries, never similarly prefixed sibling package names.
cycles 188 Return deterministic SCCs as review information, not startup-failure claims.
report 230 Keep reviewed legacy violations visible and report exact additions/removals.
main 246 Print source-only metadata and fail only on newly forbidden directions.

scripts/code_quality/source_change_guard.py

Python · Tier B

Enforce a reviewable documentation-only diff and prospective offline quality rules.

Usage

Run as scripts.code_quality.source_change_guard with an explicit Git base.

Inputs

Reviewed scope JSON, Git source snapshots and optional installed Ruff executable.

Side effects

Reads source, runs Git/Ruff only, and prints metadata; no product imports.

Cleanup

Subprocesses complete before exit and no service or database is opened.

@see scripts/code_quality/README.md

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
protected 52 Freeze frontend text and every static/template resource, including binary assets.
debt_delta 58 Compare exact stable identities with multiplicity, without line-number waivers.
documentation_parity 64 Ignore only the reviewed module docstring; preserve all symbol docs and executable AST.
complexity 83 Count executable statements per qualified function, excluding nested definitions/docs.
complexity_growth 112 Request review when a new/growing function exceeds the reviewed statement threshold.
validate_changes 122 Validate synthetic or real diff text without touching the filesystem.
normalized_tokens 147 Identify code independent of comment and whitespace movement, retaining literal values.
lint_identities 166 Key Ruff debt by rule, message and containing AST node, never physical line number.
lint 191 Check stdin under repository Ruff configuration; never fix or import product code.
main 204 Check the entire proposed maintenance diff against its immutable starting revision.

scripts/code_quality/test_results.py

Python · Tier B

Compare complete JUnit inventories without hiding failures or dropped tests.

Details

Run with --before and --after paths from the same isolated test lane. The JSON report identifies unchanged passes, failures needing review, newly skipped tests, and collection differences. Matching failure status is not a claim that the underlying cause is identical. This tool never runs or changes tests.

@see scripts/code_quality/README.md

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
TestResult 24 One test outcome, retaining parameter identity without publishing its contents.
TestResult.from_element 33 Use exact collected names, including parameters, when matching executions.
TestResult.public 51 Expose an exact identity and readable test name, without parameter values.
read_results 61 Reject empty or ambiguous reports instead of treating missing tests as success.
compare 77 Separate regressions, existing failures and inventory changes explicitly.
main 115 Compare two completed lane reports and print deterministic review evidence.
